Montréal Communiqué 


Vv 


September 10, 1970 
For release at will 


TWO MINISTRIES TO BACK 
'LOISIRS' PRE-KICKOFF 


A trans-Quebec campaign will run September 20-27 to emphasize 
the need to take advantage of leisure time in the machine-age. 

During this period, designated '‘Action-Loisirs' Week, the emphasis 
will be on the organizations and facilities which provide satisfying 
outlets for recreations. 

Quebec Cabinet Ministers Jean-Paul L'Allier (Communications) 
and Francois Cloutier (Cultural Affairs), will preside at a pre-kickoff 
news conference at 5:00 p.m., September 16th, in Corby House, 1201 
Sherbrooke West. 

"Trying to fill the hours away from jobs has become a problem 


to many people,” 


says Robert M. Cardinal, general director of the 
Association Canadienne des Centres de Loisirs. 

The ACCL and a sister organization, the Fédération des Centres 
Culturels, are principal backers of Action-Loisirs Week. Both are 
almost totally made up of French-language organizations. 

Mr. Cardinal notes, however, that the Montreal YMCA is a 
member of the ACCL and an enthusiastic participant in the province-~- 
spanning campaign. 

Pointing to the Y's participation, Mr. Cardinal suggest that 
leisure time activities could provide a promising field for pro- 


moting understanding and co-operation between Quebec's different 


language groups.
